projects.title: AQUACHIRP
projects.summary: Software-defined sonar transmitter for AUVs (SIH 2026, PS 26058 MoES/NIOT). STM32 timer + DMA streaming CW, LFM chirp, geometric, and Barker-13 waveforms.
body: Built a software-defined underwater acoustic transmitter for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles under Smart India Hackathon 2026 (Problem Statement 26058, MoES / NIOT).

Uses STM32 timer-triggered DMA streaming to synthesize Continuous Wave (CW), Linear Frequency Modulated (LFM) chirp, geometric, and Barker-13 phase-coded waveforms through an RC + CD4053B analog multiplexer + MCP6004 op-amp reconstruction chain with an onboard self-monitor feedback path.
Validated against Mackenzie and Francois-Garrison underwater acoustic propagation models. Measured bench consumption sits at ~8.1 mW at 3.3 V (~41 µJ per ping at 10 Hz PRF).
highlights: ~8.1 mW continuous bench power at 3.3 V (~41 µJ per ping at 10 Hz PRF)
Timer + DMA waveform streaming for CW, LFM chirp, geometric, and Barker-13 codes
RC + CD4053B + MCP6004 analog reconstruction chain with self-monitoring ADC path
Modeled acoustic range and absorption using Mackenzie and Francois-Garrison equations

projects.title: Smart Assistive Keyboard
projects.summary: Driverless USB-HID typing interface on a Raspberry Pi Pico W with an ST7735 TFT over SPI and 2S Li-ion pack with BMS. 1st Place at MICA 2026.
body: Designed a standalone, driverless USB-HID assistive keyboard powered by a Raspberry Pi Pico W so users with motor impairments can type on any host machine without installing custom software.

Integrates an ST7735 color TFT display over high-speed SPI for visual character selection and status readouts, calibrated analog joystick dead-zone filtering, and a portable 2S Li-ion battery pack with onboard BMS protection.
Awarded 1st Place in the Research Paper Presentation at MICA 2026.
highlights: 1st Place — Research Paper Presentation, MICA 2026
Zero-driver native USB-HID enumeration across Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android
ST7735 SPI TFT interface with dead-zone-calibrated input scanning and 2S Li-ion BMS

projects.title: Smart Motor Control & Monitoring
projects.summary: STM32F103RBT6 running five peripherals concurrently: TIM3 PWM into DRV8833, ACS712 on ADC, FT232R UART, AT24C256 on I2C, and W25Q64 on SPI with timestamped flash fault logs.
body: Engineered an integrated motor drive and protection node around the STM32F103RBT6 orchestrating five hardware peripherals simultaneously without blocking the control loop.

Drives a DRV8833 H-bridge via TIM3 PWM while sampling motor current through an ACS712 Hall-effect sensor on the ADC, streaming live telemetry over FT232R UART, storing configuration parameters in AT24C256 I2C EEPROM, and recording fault logs in W25Q64 SPI NOR flash.
Implements boot-time zero-current auto-calibration and deterministic hardware overload trip with timestamped non-volatile fault snapshots.
highlights: Five concurrent STM32 peripherals: TIM3 PWM, ADC, UART, I2C EEPROM, and SPI Flash
Boot-time ACS712 zero-offset auto-calibration and fast overcurrent cutoff
Timestamped fault history persisted in W25Q64 SPI NOR flash

projects.title: SkyGuard AI
projects.summary: Automated sensor-network quality control (SIH 2026, PS 26073 MoES/IMD). BME280 → ESP32-C3 → MQTT → FastAPI → 3-model ensemble → React. F1 0.835 at ~90 ms/decision.
body: Built an end-to-end meteorological sensor quality-control system for Smart India Hackathon 2026 (Problem Statement 26073, Ministry of Earth Sciences / IMD).

Streams environmental telemetry from a BME280 sensor over an ESP32-C3 node via MQTT into a FastAPI backend running a compact three-model anomaly detection ensemble (~265K parameters total) and a live React operator console.
Achieved an F1 score of 0.835 (precision 0.979, recall 0.728) with ~90 ms per decision latency.
highlights: F1 0.835 · Precision 0.979 · Recall 0.728 on meteorological fault injection benchmarks
~90 ms end-to-end decision latency with a lightweight ~265K-parameter 3-model ensemble
Hardware-to-cloud pipeline: BME280 → ESP32-C3 → MQTT → FastAPI → React

projects.title: REhost
projects.summary: Solar-powered ESP32 cold-chain traceability node (SIH 2026, PS 26232 MoFPI) with AES-256 encrypted readings, SHA-256 flash hash chain, MQTT sync, and six FreeRTOS tasks.
body: Developed a tamper-evident solar-powered cold-chain monitoring node for Smart India Hackathon 2026 (Problem Statement 26232, Ministry of Food Processing Industries).

Structured firmware across six concurrent FreeRTOS tasks handling sensor acquisition, AES-256 payload encryption, a local SHA-256 cryptographic hash chain in flash for offline tamper detection, and opportunistic MQTT cloud synchronization.
highlights: Six deterministic FreeRTOS tasks managing sensing, crypto, flash storage, and telemetry
AES-256 encrypted sensor payloads paired with an append-only SHA-256 hash chain in flash
Solar harvesting power budget for autonomous cold-chain transit logging

projects.title: FT232R SPI Flash Interface
projects.summary: Custom Python SPI master bit-banged over FT232R GPIO lines to read, erase, and program a W25Q64JV NOR flash chip, verified frame-by-frame in PulseView.
body: Implemented a custom SPI Mode 0 master in Python driving FT232R bit-bang GPIO pins (`CS#`, `SCK`, `MOSI`, `MISO`) to talk directly to a bare W25Q64JV 64-Mbit SPI NOR flash IC.
Verified JEDEC ID readout (`0xEF 0x40 0x17`), write-enable latching, sector erase, and 256-byte page programming waveforms using a logic analyzer and sigrok PulseView.
highlights: Direct register and opcode-level driver for W25Q64JV NOR flash without a microcontroller
Captured and verified SPI clock polarity, phase, and JEDEC ID frames in PulseView

projects.title: FT232R I2C EEPROM Interface
projects.summary: Bit-banged Python I2C master over FT232R to an AT24C256 EEPROM with open-drain pull-ups and START, STOP, and ACK/NACK timing verified in PulseView.
body: Built an I2C master from scratch in Python using FT232R GPIO lines and external open-drain pull-up resistors to read and write an AT24C256 256-Kbit EEPROM.

Hand-implementing bus arbitration, START/STOP setup and hold windows, 16-bit word addressing, and 9th-clock ACK polling provided deep hardware intuition for open-drain bus behavior under logic-analyzer inspection in PulseView.
highlights: Full bit-level implementation of I2C START, repeated START, STOP, and ACK/NACK handshakes
Verified multi-byte page writes and random reads on AT24C256 hardware in PulseView

projects.title: Vibratory Alginate Mixing Spatula
projects.summary: Ergonomic biomedical mixing instrument developed with SRM Dental College and E-Cell to reduce air-bubble entrapment in dental alginate impressions.
body: Collaborated with clinicians at SRM Dental College and SRM E-Cell to design a handheld vibratory dental spatula that eliminates micro-voids during manual alginate impression mixing.
Tuned eccentric vibration frequency and blade coupling to improve mix homogeneity while keeping grip vibration comfortable for clinical operators.
highlights: Co-designed with SRM Dental College clinicians and SRM E-Cell
Reduces air-bubble porosity during dental alginate preparation

projects.title: ELDERZAPP
projects.summary: ESP8266 Wi-Fi universal IR remote transceiver driven by an accessible, large-target mobile interface tailored for elderly users.
body: Built a Wi-Fi-connected infrared appliance bridge around an ESP8266 and high-current IR LED driver Stage, paired with a simplified high-contrast mobile app.
Captures and replays raw IR carrier pulse trains so elderly users can control TVs, set-top boxes, and air conditioners from one big-button screen.
highlights: Raw IR pulse capture and 38 kHz carrier modulation on ESP8266
Zero-clutter elder-friendly control interface over local Wi-Fi

projects.title: Laser Audio Link
projects.summary: Free-space optical analog audio transmitter and receiver from a modulated laser diode to a solar cell and PAM8403 Class-D amplifier using discrete breadboard stages.
body: Constructed a line-of-sight optical audio transmission link on a breadboard using discrete biasing components to modulate an analog audio signal onto a visible laser beam.
Recovered the modulated optical waveform across the room using a photovoltaic cell coupled through AC high-pass filtering into a PAM8403 Class-D audio amplifier driving a loudspeaker.
highlights: Pure analog optical modulation and AC-coupled photovoltaic demodulation
Clean loudspeaker reproduction across room-scale line-of-sight paths via PAM8403

Built testbenches in eSim and NGSpice to verify DC transfer characteristics, AC open-loop gain/phase, transient slew rate, and total harmonic distortion.

paragraphs: I am an electronics and embedded engineering undergraduate in Chennai who prefers datasheets, logic analyzers, and real bench numbers over black-box abstractions.

Whether I am streaming Barker-13 sonar waveforms out of an STM32 via timer-triggered DMA, bit-banging SPI and I2C from scratch in Python to watch every ACK bit in PulseView, or validating transistor-level SPICE models for IIT Bombay's FOSSEE initiative, I like knowing exactly what happens down to the pin and register level.
